suggestions: reorder joins to reduce intermediate rows
optimized_sql:
WITH period_dates AS MATERIALIZED (
    SELECT d_date_sk
    FROM date_dim
    WHERE d_year = 2002
      AND d_moy BETWEEN 1 AND (1 + 2)
)
SELECT cd.cd_gender, cd.cd_marital_status, cd.cd_education_status,
       COUNT(*) AS cnt1,
       cd.cd_purchase_estimate,
       COUNT(*) AS cnt2,
       cd.cd_credit_rating,
       COUNT(*) AS cnt3
FROM customer c
INNER JOIN customer_address ca ON c.c_current_addr_sk = ca.ca_address_sk
INNER JOIN customer_demographics cd ON cd.cd_demo_sk = c.c_current_cdemo_sk
WHERE ca.ca_state IN ('IL', 'TX', 'ME')
  AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM store_sales ss
      INNER JOIN period_dates pd ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = pd.d_date_sk
      WHERE ss.ss_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
  )
  AND (
      NOT EXISTS (
          SELECT 1
          FROM web_sales ws
          INNER JOIN period_dates pd ON ws.ws_sold_date_sk = pd.d_date_sk
          WHERE ws.ws_bill_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
      )
      AND NOT EXISTS (
          SELECT 1
          FROM catalog_sales cs
          INNER JOIN period_dates pd ON cs.cs_sold_date_sk = pd.d_date_sk
          WHERE cs.cs_ship_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
      )
  )
GROUP BY cd.cd_gender, cd.cd_marital_status, cd.cd_education_status,
         cd.cd_purchase_estimate, cd.cd_credit_rating
ORDER BY cd.cd_gender, cd.cd_marital_status, cd.cd_education_status,
         cd.cd_purchase_estimate, cd.cd_credit_rating
LIMIT 100
